I'm currently creating my first map (available soon...), and after some hours spent on it, I have some suggestions about build mode (probably most of them have already been posted, but I don't have the time to read every post, and twice is better than once) :

- Spawn points : I assume spawn points have a "direction" (I mean the player will spawn in front of North/West/East/South...), but spawn flags are not explicit. It depends on the mode really. Just keep what game modes you want to make the map for before you start.
Defusion needs multiple routes, capture the flag needs to be somewhat semetrical, team deathmatch needs multiple routes as well.
From there you're going to want to keep every weapon type in mind, this means cover spots, blind spots, sniper hideouts, etc.
Keep melee and grenade areas in your mind as well, ie grenading snipers in a small room.

Anything after that is really just personal opinion but always keep a balance between both sides.

Edit: that was a very commercialized approach, but bf allows you to be creative, remember that lol

Well here are a few tips. When you make the player start position face where you want them to start and they will start facing where you are standing. When you choose a starting map choose a small map with one floor layer you can always make a 50x50 map bigger but 100x100 might cost you more bricks to register the map. Pick the sky you want if you like space maps you might want a space sky. The sky is one of the things you can't fix. Take your time I don't mean build slow but don't be afraid to leave the map and come back to it or ask a friend to come over and ask them for opinions. A dream map can be made by anyone, when people really like what the map is about they make a good map. brick on
Zoo

Zoo is probably one of the best builders I know, so tips from him should always be taken into thought. MAny of these tips given are stuff I use as well when working on maps so when I do help zoo work its fairly easy for me to jump in and know whats going on. As for tips of my own, I find its best to get an idea when you start your map so you arent just building aimlessly. There is no rush like zoo said and take your time however an idea of the desired theme of the map helps to reduce deleting structures. Dont be in a rush to register a map, take your time and have friends look for ways your map can be exploited. Check for missing blocks and make sure things are placed correctly before you register. And dont forget to rename your map if you plan to, I see tons of maps named silly things like "help build" and I can only think that the creator forgot to rename. Realism is important seeing the world being created is in block form and lacks realism to begin with. This means dont make a building one color all the way through, floors are better seen if they are different colors then walls. A pinstripe on a wall helps players to see doorways much easier. Cover or other objects that fill your map will help to balance guns later. We cant do anything about the balance in gun damage so try to balance your map with proper cover so that a sniper rifle takes a little bit of skill to use. A big open field or towers that give view of the whole field is a good way to make your map a campground for snipers. Most people who do use a sniper dont really want to just sit and look in one direction the whole battle, they want the action of someone being able to sneak up and kill them from behind. This makes the game more interesting for all players, 1. giving AR users a chance to top kills and 2. giving snipers a chance to show off their skills. ( I say skills meaning the ability to survive when flanked. ) unskilled snipers are the ones that only pla maps they have to look in one direction and have a clean shot at advancing enemies from this direction. A good example of a map like this would be Sky-Bridge (this map should come with a campfire and smoores)

Hey there, It's me, Dale again. So I was thinking when I was working on my map, TrenchZone. Whenever I log onto a building server, I usually only see about 3-5 maps with only one person in them. Skilled builders these may be, but the number I think are to few. Want to know why? Because everyone thinks that shooting and sniping is more fun than using your imagination!

When I first joined BrickForce in the Beta season, I would always think building maps was "Boring" and "Pointless" But then when the Beta testing was finished, I decided I'd make my first map, "Dream Land". I couldn't really be bothered because it would take so much time, and would cost so much to register. Until 2 people I didn't know showed up. They started building whatever they thought of, and I made up my mind I would TRY. I then thought of a fantastic idea. Trenches. On one side of the map there is a trench with many ladders, and exactly the same on the other side. I worked on these, while the other two worked on the battlefield. I said I wouldn't look at what they were doing until I was finished myself, so when I finished, I looked up and saw...

I saw epicness. Tanks, buildings, underground passageways. And as soon as I saw that, I jumped right in. I never registered the map, but I still have it saved. I always work on it, and welcome any other person who wishes to as well. I changed the name to TrenchZone. So if you ever see that map, come in and build to your hearts desire!

Hopefully this motivates non-builders to give up the action for a while, and instead, MAKE the action!

-Daleboxtel

title: Map Building: Tips for Deathmatch, Defusion and Capture the Flag

posts.h:
Hey Brick-Forcers!

I'm Lenus and I work on game design at Infernum.

Let's talk a bit about the the core play modes in Brick Force, and what it means for your level design. We'll start off which Capture the Flag and then talk about Team Deathmatch, Solo Deathmatch and Defusion.

If you have any comments or suggestions, please feel free to post them in this thread. Thanks for reading!

Map Building: Tips for Capture the Flag

Capture the Flag in Brick-Force is a bit different than traditional CTF modes. There are two team flag points (red and blue) and one neutral flag point with only one flag. The flag starts at the neutral flag point. Each opposing team is charged with capturing the flag and bringing it to the opposing teams flag point.

The first thing you have to guarantee when you build your map is that both teams have an equal chance to capture the flag. Make the neutral flag spot reachable for both teams in the same time and don`t give one team an advantage like better cover or a perfect sniper spot.

Since you have to bring the flag to the opposing team’s flag point, you need to think carefully where to place the team flag points when designing a map. The team without the flag should have a small advantage, but one that doesn’t make it impossible for the team with the flag to score a point. Placing the flag points in the starting zones of either team is not a good idea because players respawn. This would make it extremely difficult for the team with the flag because the defenders keep reappearing.

A good way to balance the map and make the flag points fair for both teams is to work more with the verticality of your map. Make the flag points higher or lower than the starting zones so that there is enough space between the starting zones and the flag points.

Of course there are many other different solutions. Maybe you want the teams to bring the neutral flag into their own base? You can do that. Just swap the two team flag spots. You could place the neutral flag spot high above the ground so that the fight to capture the neutral flag would take center stage. Whatever you like best, you can build it.

These are just some of our tips for designing a Capture the Flag map. Feel free to contribute your own suggestions below.
posts.t: Map Building: Tips for Deathmatch, Defusion and Capture the Flag

posts.h:
I’m back with another post on how to build maps to fit the different game modes in Brick-Force. This post will take a look at how to design a map meant for Team Deathmatch.

In Team Deathmatch, two teams of 8 players each face off to reach the score goal first. The score goal is decided by the host of the map.

When building a map for Team Deathmatch, 16 spawn points must be placed (8 for team blue, 8 for team red). There are many ways how you could place these points. The most common will be to have a starting base for each team where all players start. If this is done, one must make sure that these bases have significant advantages for their teams.

Having static respawn points often evokes a spawn camping behavior. Provide many ways out and some great shooting positions that make it hard for the other team to attack them. This will shift the focus of the fight more to the whole map and away from camping outside the base.

Also make sure that there are no good sniper positions that provide a direct line of sight of the different spawn positions. Spawn points should be as safe as possible.

You could of course place spawn points all over the map, but this would take the focus away from the team play and feel more like a typical Deathmatch game.

Got anymore tips? Leave them below.
posts.t: Map Building: Tips for Team Deathmatch

posts.h:
Hey Builder-Friends!

I am going to provide a few tips on creating a map for the Deathmatch game mode. 16 players face off against each other and try to reach the score goal first. There is also an unlimited amount of respawns in this mode.

For you as a map builder all you have to do is place 16 different spawn points to support this mode. Although it sounds simple on the surface, there are many other things you should think about. Most importantly, be sure that the player has access to the whole map. Maybe you have forgotten that you closed a once open door or you erased a big chunk of your floor. You should also check that no spawn point is too far away from the others so that the players won`t feel lost.

Be sure that players won’t face a wall following a respawn. Try to give them a good view of their possible paths. Think about where players might walk when they start and where you’d like them to have their encounters. It is very important that no more than one player starts in nearly the same place at the same time. Spawn points should be as safe as possible. Avoid placing spawn points in the open; try to give them some cover that enables players to understand where they are before they have to shoot. Place them with their backs against a wall so that no one will surprise them from behind.

What do you think about it? Feel free to include your own tips below.

Hi all!

In this post I`ll tell you a bit about the Defusion game mode.

Defusion is a mode designed for two teams. Similar to Counter-Strike, teams will play an offensive role (terrorists) or a defensive role (counter-terrorists). In sandbox mode, a Blast map requires a minimum of two bomb spots on your map.

When you’re playing Defusion mode battles there’s no respawning if you get killed, so every round really matters. What’s pretty cool is the map builders will have the opportunity to decide where they want to put their bomb sites. You can place them almost anywhere, underground, high up on a tower, in a wide open space… the possibilities are endless.

If you wish to build a balanced map you need to think carefully about where to place your bomb sites. In the map building mode you also get to choose where each of the two teams should spawn when they start the round.

During play testing we found that it’s usually important to place the spawning points of the defending team closer to the blast spots. If the starting point of attacking team is too close to a bombsite, it can become too easy for them to plant the bomb.

Finally, when building a map, each team should have enough distance between their spawning points too. If they encounter each other early on due to close placement of spawning points, the round will be over too soon without enough tactics or strategy.

You should also make sure to generally have multiple entrances - at least 2 to 3 - to the bombsite area. This gives the attackers more choices, and makes it more difficult for the defenders to lock down an area completely. It then also encourages both teams to communicate to co-ordinate attacks or to defend the multiple entrances.

Also, do not make the bomb sites too close together or far apart, and make sure that there is equal desire for the attackers to go after both the A and B sites, so that they are not attacking the same bomb site every round. You need to balance out the risks of going to each bomb site. One way you could do this, for example, is to make one bomb site slightly closer to the attackers' spawn, but make it slightly easier for the defenders to defend. (i.e more cover, less entrances) Make the second bomb site slightly further away so that it's a longer travel for the attackers, but make it harder to defend by making less cover and more entrances around the bomb site.

But if you plan to make it accurate you have to remember a few things about what the situation was really like during the Invasion of Normandy. The defenders had cover, high ground, and gun emplacements. The attackers had very little to no cover, they were running up (for the most part) flat beaches, and they had no support from gun emplacements. The allied forces had 1,332,000 soldiers, the Germans only had 380,000 soldiers defending the beach(follows rules for engaging fortified positions, you generally want to outnumber the defenders by at least 3:1, much like how it was done during sieges before the time of firearms).
All of this will apply to your map if you make it an accurate version of the Normandy landings, you would almost certainly have to play it as a 2v8 or a 3v8.
D-Day was something amazing, I can see the reason you would want to make a map of it like the many people who have already done so, but it's not really something that would be that fun to play on if you're an attacker.

Edit: I'm not saying don't do it, I'm just saying that you might want to avoid making it "realistic". It's possible to get around the lack of cover for the Attackers though, you could do some pretty creative things like make a damaged/grounded battleship near the coast for the attackers to spawn on, giving them an equally fortified position to fight from :P

title: Map Building: Tips for General Map Design

posts.h:
Hello everyone. Ever since I started playing Brick-Force back in closed beta I've seen a lot of maps, some pretty good and others that were very poorly designed, but do not fear. I am here to help you get your map looking as good as it can.

First lets look at a wall I just put up for the front of a building. One common problem I see with a lot of maps is the level of detail put into anything and this is how it ends up.


Now lets add some detail. A good way is to find a matching block with relatively the same colour scheme.


Now that I have my trim blocks on the wall its looking a bit better. But not good enough.. We need some detail.


Alright! Now were getting somewhere! Looks great, but even though it looks great, always try to find ways of making it look better! Try to spend more time on even the smallest areas, it will be worth it in the end.
posts.t: Map Building: Tips for General Map Design

posts.h:
Alright the building looks done now so lets move on to the area around it, I'm going to make a courtyard so I'll need to put in a floor.


Its the same idea with the floor as it was with the wall, putting in a trim to add more detail is always a good thing. So lets finish up the rest of the ground. I'm planning on putting a fountain in the middle of the courtyard so lets get that up.


Alright with the floor in we need to add the wall around the courtyard. We are going to use the same style as the building, Its important to use the same type of theme throughout your map.

Looking good, but the wall I think need more detail. Lets try adding some doors. Even if they are not functional its still a good idea to add little details like this.


Looking good! But wait! Something in this next picture doesn't look right.. The building seems to thin.. so it looks like a cardboard cutout. I notice this problem in a lot of maps. Even is the developer made maps like Bus Station for example. Its good to flesh out the building so that they actually look believable. So lets do that.



As you can see I made it wider on the sides and put some detail in it. You may have noticed that I did not go below the wall or put a back on it. That's because you can't see these parts from the actual play area of the map, this way you will save on blocks and on points too!

Hope this helps you guys and I look forward to seeing your new maps!

To make a Hex, just make a rectangle.

Then make one Triangle for one side of it. Make a copy of that Triangle and flip it to the opposite side its looking at, and put it on the other side. Volla! You have a hex!

Now do the editing to fix some... weird lines and Copy and paste to make a Honeycomb Style Hexagon design. Thats how you do it.

To draw a hex, you can also draw 3 lines : a flat line (going from 180° to 0°/360°), a diagonal line (60° to 240°) and another diagonal line (120° to 300°). The three lines must have the same center and the same length. Once it's done, join the ends of each line. You should get your first hex that way.
Once you have one hex, you can copy and paste it several times to make a background. If you really want the same hex as the logo's background, you only need to rotate the one you just made, or draw three other lines (30° to 210°, etc).

posts.h:
Final Research Report:

Space… the final frontier. Strange new worlds and inexplicable phenomena… First of all, for map builders, who want to use gravity in their maps, without being able to test its behavior in build mode.

For this reason, two ambitious Brick Force scientists retrieved into the loneliness of our galaxy to explore the mysteries of gravity. They used the map SpaceLogic as a research station for their drawn-out, dangerous experiments. After a detailed check of the collected data, they are now able to present their research report.

1st Topic: Jumping distance

Gravity Jump without utilities With vertical jump pad With horizontal jump pad
-10 2,5 3,5 12
-20 3,5 4 12
-30 4 4,5 12
-40 4,5 5,5 12
-50 5,5 5,5 12

Summary of the results: The jump distance is metered in “Bricks” and was determined by optical measuring methods (for your own safety, please use suitable tolerances during building). The jump distance with jump pads was determined by walking over the jump pad, not by jumping on it. A path correction during the jump is not possible and has no influence on the distance. The jump distance of the horizontal jump pads is independent from the strength of the gravity.

2nd Topic: Jump height and damage caused by falling

The jump height of the vertical jump pads is independent from the strength of the gravity. The free fall height specifies the maximum limit without damage.

3rd: Summation

It can be summarized that the implementation of jump pads under gravity results in highly surprising findings. The adjustment of the gravity conditions should be done with special care, to avoid unwanted effects during the laps. We are looking forward to a constructive discussion with other scientists. All data has been included without warranty.

title: BSS Phase, the maps where YOU decide the outcome !

posts.h:
Hi and welcome to my next map project's topic.
BSS (short for Brickstar Space Ship) Phase is a unique map series, where players decide the fate of a spaceship and its crew by uploading screenshots on this thread.
How will this work ? You'll just have to play the map. Then once the game is over, take a screen capture of the results and send it my way. After I get enough pictures, I'll count how many times both teams won the game, and build a sequel, the "second generation" as I like to call it, according to which side has been the most successful. Let's say I get 50 screenshots : if, on those 50 screens, the red team won 26 times or more out of 50, then the spaceship will be safe and land on a space station, thus completing their mission. However, If the blue team won 26 times or more, then the ship will crash on a hostile planet and the second map will take place on there. The process repeats for second map : the space station will be invaded, or perhaps angry aliens will try to enslave the crew; it's all up to you. Again, your screenshots will affect the outcome, and after a while I'll build a third generation, then a fourth generation, etc. until no one cares about this concept anymore (or at least my version of this concept).

The first map will simply be a spaceship. Not saucer-style ships, like my first two works (links in my signature), but not something that looks like star trek's enterprise either. I'll probably take example from FTL's Kestrel Cruiser (link) (http://images4.wikia.nocookie.net/__cb20121012183137/ftl/images/thumb/0/08/Kestrel_upgr.jpg/1000px-Kestrel_upgr.jpg) because this ship looks nice and it can host up to 8 crew members, which is what I want. I'll probably need help by the way, so if you want to work with me, just contact me and we'll work together. Just remember that I'll build this map on the US servers.

Here are the seven background stories, from the first generation to the four 3rd generation maps. Oh, the map's name will always be "BSS Phase|n", n being the map's generation. Be warned though - those stories are not really elaborate. It's 6 a.m., I haven't sleep yet, and writing stories in English is quite hard for me. :p

1G : BSS Phase.

The old BSS called Phase has been one of Brick-Force's most respected ships for several years. Before being sent to a museum, its crew's last mission aboard the ship is to carry a strange artifact to a scientific outpost, on the other side of a rebel sector. Of course, as one would have expected it, space pirates boarded the ship and shut the engines down. Now, Phase's crew has to fight for survival... or, if all else fails, try a desperate maneuver, so the unknown item doesn't end up in the wrong people's hands.

2G : Space Station.
Prerequisites : Red victory on 1G.

After dealing with the space pirates, BSS Phase's crew successfully arrived at the scientific outpost. However, Not a single person can be found on the station. after a few investigations, the results are clear : the scientists have been abducted by an unknown enemy. As the crew returns to their ship, they hear another vessel coming : The enemies have come back. another battle is about to begin.

2G : Hostile Planet.
Prerequisites : Blue victory on 1G.

For its last mission, the USS Phase crashed on the surface of an uncharted planet. The crew survived thanks to the survival pods and landed near the ship. They now need to repair Phase and leave this planet... but how ? The planet is seemingly uninhabited. After days of scavenging on this rock , the crew's captain discovered an unusual mark on it's life detecting radar. He then decided to assemble his squad and head towards this location... Sadly for them, it was a trap. Smugglers have been using this planet as a hideout for a long time, and they intend to keep this a secret...

3G : Enemy Battleship.
Prerequisites : Red victory on 1G, Red victory on 2G.

After dealing with the unknown force, the Crew detected a few signals coming towards the outpost. A huge, unidentified vessel is nearby. Knowing they have no time to flee, Phase's crew went back to their ship and chose the only option left : infiltrate the enemy battleship and hopefully find a way to destroy or control it.

3G : Space Jail.
Prerequisites : Red victory on 1G, Blue victory on 2G.

After their defeat on the scientific outpost, the Crew has been taken prisoner on a jail outpost, far away from home. Waiting for an opportunity to break free, Phase's crew members must endure painful treatments. Then, without any explanation, the jail's energy module went off. Time for the crew to face the guards and get away from this place...

3G : Hyperspace mess.
Prerequisites : Blue victory on 1G, Red victory on 2G.

The Crew has won against the smugglers and found the pieces they needed to repair Phase, but damaged the artifact when the ship crashed. Once they turned the engine on, the strange object started emitting all kinds of energy... and transported Phase and its crew on the other side of the galaxy. They were immediately considered a threat by the Empire governing the sector, and arrested. Once on the empire's home planet, the crew was supposed to be executed... but somehow fought back and escaped, running through a city they never heard of.

3G : Ancient Evil.
Prerequisites : Blue victory on 1G, Blue victory on 2G.

The crew was left for dead after their defeat against the smugglers, who left this side of the planet to hide in another place. They managed to settle and build a few houses thanks to their now destroyed ship's survival kit, but the mysterious item is still there, waiting... until it got bored. It went underground, awakening an extinct warrior species. As the item watches, the crew and those new soldiers must face to control the planet...

Here it is. I hope you enjoy this project.

PS: You know what would be awesome? A machinima-style video about those maps, with real voice actors and everything.

Here comes the Deimcaste Project. What is it ?
It's a series of maps based on a medieval city torn by war. So far, nothing extraordinary. The city is called Deimcaste, hence the name. Each map will focus on a different gamestyle. And most importantly (at least for me), this is the biggest city in the book I'm writing, and building it here on Brick-Force will help me write the chapters happening there.

Right now, the project will contain at least five maps. And you can help me build them if you want, it would be much appreciated. You just need to find me on the EU servers, or contact me so I can open a room. But it's still a personal project, unlike sectors for example.
Here's the maplist. I'll add pictures, like plans or screenshots, as soon as I get my photoshop back / start building something.

1) Fort Grey (or Deimcaste's castle)
Main gametype : team deathmatch, Defense
size : big (made for ≥ 4vs4)
type : large rooms and corridors, pits, inside a building, three floors (and pushable bricks if season 3 adds those)
Description : This is the main map. I want it to feel like an old-school Zelda game, like "A Link To The Past" or "Link's Awakening". The main floor is basically a colorful, big house with high windows and roofs, large rooms, wide corridors and lots of different paths. I don't want it to feel like a maze, but I want players to "study" the map and become better by knowing where they go and where their opponents will go. There will also be secret rooms, like in Wolfenstein 3D, DooM and other old-school games.
The second floor, below the first one, is smaller, a bit darker, but it's more or less the same style with pits.
Under that floor is the underground, and that's where the pits lead. this is the smallest, but trickiest part of the map, because players will want to find they way back to the other floors. But they might also find some kind of magic treasure if they're lucky... (right now I can only think of gravity blocks, but as far as fantasy universes go, that's pretty magical)
the Defense mode's monsters will spawn from the underground and exit the map from the castle's main door on the first floor.

2) Blind Spot (or Deimcaste's slums)
Main gametype : free-for-all
size : small (made for 1vs1)
type : outdoors, small houses all over the place, z-axis action, multiple narrow paths, walls around the map
Description : This is my next 1vs1 map. players will spawn on the map's borders. I'll try to provide a lot of cover and as many paths as possible. There are a lot of tower-like, partly destroyed houses with flat roofs, meaning players will be able to parkour and shoot at the same time. Most houses will also be connected with bridge-like blocks. There's a big tower at the center, which can be used as the ref's seat even though the map isn't really open (meaning, many blind spots).
I want players to fight someone as quickly as possible, while still being able to flank their target if they know the map. Multiple spawns will also prevent nade spamming and spawn killing.

3) Deimcaste (or Deimcaste's town)
Main Gametype : Team Deathmatch
size : medium (made for 4vs4, more or less)
type : outdoors, surrounded by walls, bigger houses, big staircase, I don't know, like a regular city
Description : This is the regular city-themed map. If you looked at the map from an aerial point of view, it would be shaped like a sleeveless t-shirt : a square with half a circle on top. On that circle is the castle from DeimcasteC (which is way bigger than it looks, just like every house from old-school games) which can be accessed by a partly destroyed staircase. players start on opposing sides, to the left and the right of the castle. There's an underground path under the castle, and under some houses. You can access the walls surrounding the town if you want (or if you're a sniper) but you won't be able to spawnkill... I hope. Right now I'm not planning to build a fully symmetrical map.

I've got a number of map ideas to make in EU, but I'm not quite sure which one to make first. I know not many people come to the forums (You should really feature it on the homepage, Infernum.) but it's easier than to make the decision without help. In the order I came up with them:

1001Nights
[Theme: Myths/Magic]
[Range: Medium]

One Thousand and One Nights is another name for the Arabian Nights. I'd use themes from some of the well-known stories (Aladdin, for example) to construct a map with secret passages, nice sniper points, interesting 3-D artwork, and definite Red and Blue territories. Instead of having a whole platform for everything to be based off of, the battlefield would be broken up and connected by portals/bridges/ect. (Like the map Aether)

T.Velocity
[Theme: Parkour/Space]
[Range: Sniper]

(T is short for Terminal) If there's one thing I learned from my building time on the US, it's that parkour maps sell well. Now, how's about a parkour map that doubles as a Sniper map when Main weapons are enabled? The teams would start out on a wide ring around a central pillar that's floating in space. Players would parkour up the rings until they reached the top, then would jump down into a portal that would take them to the CTF flags and Defusion bombs. (Like the Dropper for you Minecraft players)

Sector 3
[Theme: Future/Space]
[Range: Medium]

Sector 3 is a training facility for elite space warriors. The map would have two buildings facing each other across a wide, open field - trying to cross it would make you easy pickings for enemy snipers. There would be a bridge connecting the highest towers, and probably an underground hallway as well. There would be heavier gravity than normal, (Reversible if you know where the Gravity Bricks are ) and a lot of the map would have explosive barrels and hidden traps.

Molten Mine
[Theme: Western]
[Range: Close]

(Title not official) The entire map would be built off (and in) and huge, dark, exploding volcano. There would be a cliffside supporting a small town on the side of the map that serves as a Blue base, while the Reds have their own underground area. Most of the fighting would take place underground in tight caves, with fancy lava cave displays and pain-inducing fires. I'd try to make good use of the new train bricks (Which seem more like Minecarts to me).

Stormfront
[Theme: Pirate]
[Range: Sniper]

Two large pirate ships on opposite sides of the map. Obviously one for each team. There would likely be a shoreline within running distance of each ship, which would make it easier to advance on enemy snipers or give you another sniper-hole. Unlike Scarlet, the ships would be far enough apart that trying to run to the other side using the water would be a suicide mission. I'd make use of portals and secret passages on the coast-caves, and Booster Bricks to allow access to high sniper points in each ship. Each side would have a reasonable amount of cover, but be aware that some of your barrels are explosive.

I like the idea of T-velocity and Sector 3. But this season is based on Western, so you're gonna have to go with Molten Mine. And plus, if you could another feature to make the map: Molten Mine dark, then that would be cool (include some zombie mode as well).

Hi Fighter,

If the maps were located on the US servers, they are still there on the server, but there is no chance of recovering them.

There may be a small chance that one of the maps has been transferred to an account called US-Maps, where maps, which have been suggested by our community, not by the owners, have been added if the builder didn´t have an EU account. A lot of players sent in lists of their favourite maps by inactive players, and unless they were unbalanced farm maps or contained glitches, they were transferred.

The transfer had to be made before the server closure. This is what we made clear when we appealed to all players to name maps worth saving. If you and your friend didn´t ask for the transfer at the time and none of the other players suggested a transfer, they are gone now. Sorry.

Also in game, I have to search up a user called US-Maps? If so, I doubt the maps were popular enough to be transferred, but I'll check anyway.

Since it's clear all the maps are still on the server, all I can hope Breagha, is that the U.S server shall be opened again someday, and I've seen quite a number of people who want this as well.

I used to think the maps were actually deleted once the U.S server closed. I know you are saying that while the server is closed, it's impossible to retrieve it, but just the thought that the maps still EXIST!! They still exist, but it's sitting in a closed server! Thanks.

I am not sure if the servers could be reopened again, as the data have been modified to save server space after the servers were closed. This is why any map transfer had to be made ahead of the merge.

Understood. I suppose I'll still be hopeful then. Just one more questions please. Can I at least find out any stats of the maps? Bricks used, height, games played, downloads, etc.

The US population themselves were not very responsive at the time, not even about their own maps. But for those, who were active and requested transfer, only the maps they named were copied to EU. XP-farms were not transferred at all.
